answer: An agent market requires each identity to lock a refundable bond for 30 days, then allocates scarce job bids in proportion to bonded funds. Agents named ember, velvet, and willow follow the same rule: splitting one bond among a thousand identities earns no extra share of bids. To capture more work, an attacker must commit more capital and forgo its use for a month; generating names alone buys no influence.
